overview: This House resolution directs the Clerk of the House to tell the Senate that a quorum (enough members to conduct business) is present and that the House is ready to begin its work. It is a routine notice the House sends at the start of each new session of Congress. The House agreed to it on January 6, 2026.
for: Supporters say it is a standard step that formally lets the two chambers begin working together in the new session.
against: Critics say it is a ceremonial procedural measure that doesn't change any law or spending.
